description: Random-mutation hill climbing (RMHC) improves one candidate solution at a time. It copies the current genome, applies one random mutation, and keeps the copy if its cost is not worse; because it accepts equal costs, it can move across flat regions (*plateaus*). Optionally it restarts from a new random genome after a given number of steps without strict improvement, and it returns the best genome of all restarts. It needs only a mutation operator, so it works for any genome type, but it can stop at a *local optimum*, a solution that no single mutation improves; it has no optimality guarantee. In this crate it is also the population-of-one case of rolling-horizon planning and one of the local searchers of the memetic algorithm.

papers.authors: Thor V. A. N. Olesen, Dennis T. T. Nguyen, Rasmus Berg Palm, Sebastian Risi
papers.title: Evolutionary Planning in Latent Space
